decisions.rationale: Quality, net cash and a peer discount justify owning it. But earnings sit on peak-cycle margins, EV/Sales and P/B are above their 5-year highs, and beta is 2.39. Normalised earnings could be far lower. A 3% starter caps the cyclical downside. The portfolio is all cash, so no limits bind.

Target and stop are roughly symmetric, yet the earnings gap risk is asymmetric: beta 2.45, price 71.3% above the 200-day MA, EV/EBITDA above its 5y max. A guidance disappointment would likely gap the shares through the stop. The reward-to-risk does not justify a tactical slot, even with an empty portfolio.
